Notice that the logarithms share the same base.

First, we apply the power rule to the *second* term to make the coefficient in front of each logarithm the same:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+\frac{1}{3}{log}_{5}⁡(8{x}^{3}) & =3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+{log}_{5}⁡((8{x}^{3})^{1/3}) & =3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+{log}_{5}⁡(2x) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we combine the logarithms using the product rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\cdot 2x) & =3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡({x}^{3}) & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing this equation in its equivalent exponential form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{3})} & ={5}^{3} \\ {x}^{3} & =125\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve this equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3} & =125 \\ x & =\sqrt[3]{125} \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=5$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{{5}^{2}}{2})+\frac{1}{3}{log}_{5}⁡(8\cdot {5}^{3}) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{25}{2})+{log}_{5}⁡((8\cdot {5}^{3})^{1/3}) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{25}{2})+{log}_{5}⁡(({2}^{3}\cdot {5}^{3})^{1/3}) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{25}{2})+{log}_{5}⁡(10) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(\frac{25}{2}\cdot 10) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(125) & \overset{?}{=}3 \\ 3 & =3.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=5$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=5$ only."
